title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics (v13)
author: Priya Natarajan
description:
Motivation: reduce wasted compute from padding in continuous/dynamic batching by grouping requests by sequence length buckets and applying a padding-cost-aware bucketing policy. This PR introduces a production-safe, tunable heuristic that: (1) derives sequence-length buckets from runtime request distributions (percentile-based), (2) applies an objective that trades increased queueing delay against padded token cost, and (3) integrates bucket-awareness into scheduler kernel selection and KV-cache reuse.

What changed (high-level):
- New seqlen bucketing module (runtime/batching/seqlen_bucketer.go) that computes buckets from a sliding-window histogram and exposes a small API for candidate bucket sets. Buckets are represented as inclusive ranges.
- Padding minimization heuristic implemented in the batcher: choose bucket set that minimizes padded_tokens_cost + alpha * queue_delay_cost, where alpha is configurable per-customer via route config.
- Scheduler integration: bucket tag added to batch metadata so kernel selection can prefer specialized kernels for common sequence lengths and avoid high-overhead path for short sequences.
- KV cache affinity: when possible, requests in the same bucket reuse KV cache shards to reduce KV cache misses on long-context workloads.
- Migration/compatibility: new heuristics are opt-in behind feature flag DYN_BATCH_SEQLEN_V13. Default is OFF for Dedicated until we finish canary.
- Tests: unit tests for bucketer, end-to-end integration test in perf-canary harness, and benchmarks measuring padded tokens and throughput.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc referenced (ENG-7211)
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Perf regression tests added to perf-canary
- [x] Feature-flag guarded for staged rollout

Benchmarks: On internal perf-canary using a mixed web+assistant workload (P50 seqlen 64, P90 512):
- Mean padded tokens per batch reduced by ~28% (est. 0.22 tokens/token cost)
- Throughput +6% for GPU V100 pools at target SLOs (when alpha tuned to 0.8)
- Latency P95 unchanged within noise for low-latency routes; small +3ms median queuing for long-tail routes when aggressiveness increased

Risks and mitigations:
- Increased head-of-line blocking if alpha is set too high — mitigated by conservative defaults and per-route override.
- KV-cache shard affinity may cause uneven memory pressure — added monitoring and backpressure hooks.

Rollout plan: staged canary on perf-canary -> 5% traffic on hosted API next week -> increase to 25% after 48h stable metrics -> Dedicated opt-in in next release.

Related: previous iterations and experiments are in ENG-6342 and PRs about seqlen heuristics (see changelog).

review_comments: Marco Alvarez: Nice work. Can we make alpha configurable per-route and default to 0.5? Also add a metric for padded_tokens_saved per-route.
Priya Natarajan: Addressed — alpha is per-route with fallback to global default. Added padded_tokens_saved and padded_token_ratio metrics and exposed them in batching_metrics.yaml.
Jia Chen: The KV-cache affinity logic looks good, but I'm concerned about shard hotspots. Please add a circuit-breaker to fall back to no-affinity when memory pressure is high.
Priya Natarajan: Added a fallback and an observable (kv_affinity_fallback_count). Also added a small e2e test simulating shard pressure.
Lena Fisher: CI flaky test 'TestBatchingLatency' failed on first run; reran and passed. Please add a comment where we assert latency bounds.
Priya Natarajan: Added explicit latency assertion in integration test and documented acceptable bounds in docs/ops/batching.md.
release_notes: Improves dynamic batching by grouping requests into sequence-length buckets to reduce padding overhead and improve throughput. Opt-in via feature flag DYN_BATCH_SEQLEN_V13. Adds per-route alpha tuning, new batching metrics, and KV-cache affinity with fallback.
